title: Micro‑Beta Readiness Heuristics & SLA Scaling Log
content:
Purpose:
This working notebook collects the heuristics, lightweight KPI trackers, and short runbook fragments for the micro‑beta (small cohort) that precedes our broader pilot. Goal: validate traffic economics (latency vs cost), operator burden, and degradation/fallback behavior for the hosted + dedicated routing mix.

Document status and usage notes:
- Living doc: use for standups and preflight signoffs.
- Meant to be concise: link out to deep dive spreadsheets for raw telemetry.
- If you update thresholds below, add a one‑line rationale and date.

High‑level micro‑beta plan (summary):
1) Phase A (internal alpha, 100 users synthetic + 20 internal): validate end‑to‑end telemetry and tracing (2 weeks).
2) Phase B (micro‑beta cohort, 500–2,000 monthly active users): soft traffic ramp; enable dedicated routing for heavy prompt families; run cost profiling (2–4 weeks).
3) Phase C (pilot gating): open to selected external customers; measure steady‑state economics and SLA adherence (4–8 weeks).

Traffic economics KPIs (compact tracker) — use these as go/no‑go gates:
- KPI: Median p95 latency (inference, API surface) | Owner: Marcus Liu | Target: p95 <= 220ms | Baseline: 180ms | Trigger to act: p95 > 280ms for 30m | Action: reduce concurrency / route to fallback model + page SRE
- KPI: Cost per 1k tokens (hosted mix) | Owner: Ravi Desai | Target: <$0.60/1k tokens | Baseline: $0.53 | Trigger: > $0.80 for sustained 24h | Action: enable quantized model variant and update billing note
- KPI: Error rate (5xx + timeouts) | Owner: Elena Kwon | Target: <0.5% | Baseline: 0.15% | Trigger: >= 1% 15m | Action: rollback recent routing change, initiate incident runbook
- KPI: Model quality regression (eval pass rate on sentinel prompts) | Owner: Priya Shah | Target: >= 95% pass rate | Baseline: 98% | Trigger: drop below 92% | Action: pause rollout and run offline evals + QA signoff
- KPI: Operator interrupts (pager incidents/week) | Owner: Ava Martinez | Target: <= 2/week | Baseline: 0–1 | Trigger: > 4/week | Action: evaluate runbook gaps, add automated mitigations

Compact readiness checklist (pre‑phase B signoff):
- [ ] Telemetry verified: request IDs flow through gateway -> runtime -> tracing UI (sample traces verified).
- [ ] Canary traffic generator configured and scheduled (low/med/high curves).
- [ ] Dedicated pool sizing for expected peak defined (+20% buffer).
- [ ] Fallback model variants uploaded and smoke‑tested (latency + simple QA prompts).
- [ ] Billing/usage metering test completed end‑to‑end (billing tags validated).
- [ ] Customer comms templates ready (status page prepopulated, short FAQ).
- [ ] Security review complete for data retention and KMS usage.

Runbook fragments (quick actions):
- Slow p95 spike (immediate):
  1. Identify top request routes (console top N routes).
  2. If spike isolated to single route, reduce traffic weight to 20% and re‑route to fallback.
  3. If system‑wide, enable emergency throttle and flip to dedicated reserve capacity (if available).
  4. Notify product Ops and SRE on Slack #prodops‑incidents.

- Quality regression seen in evals:
  1. Stop progressive rollout (hold at current percent).
  2. Run focused evaluation harness against morning/nightly prompt set.
  3. If issue reproducible, rollback model version; if transient, open investigation ticket and continue monitoring.

- Cost surge detected (unexpected):
  1. Cross‑check token distribution by customer and route.
  2. Identify prompt families with heavy sampling; apply client‑side prompt guidance if possible.
  3. Activate cheaper quantized variant for non‑latency‑sensitive routes.
  4. Alert finance owner for cost anomaly explanation.

Preflight tests (to run weekly during micro‑beta ramp):
- Latency/responsiveness sweep (synthetic): 3 profiles (short, mid, long sequences).
- Cold‑cache vs warm‑cache throughput: measure kv cache hit rate impact and tail latency.
- Billing tags sampling: verify 5 customer ids across environments map correctly.
- Network partition simulation (region fallback): confirm smart routing fails over within SLO window.

Tuning heuristics (practical rules we've found useful):
- Prefer routing by route family (prompt shape + expected sequence length) rather than by customer to reduce cache dilution.
- Default starting concurrency for dedicated pools: 0.7 * single‑GPU theoretical throughput (safe headroom for heterogeneity).
- When cost > target, prefer quantized variant for long‑sequence families before throttling endpoints where UX degrades dramatically.
- Use p95 trending over 30m windows rather than instantaneous p95 to avoid flip‑flop.

Ownership & communication matrix (who to call first):
- Product Ops lead (owner): Ava Martinez — overall go/no‑go, customer comms
- Runtime SRE: Marcus Liu — latency/scale issues
- Serving infra: Ravi Desai — capacity and model variants
- Quality lead: Priya Shah — evaluation/behavior regressions
- Finance contact: Liza Kim — cost anomalies and forecasting

Unresolved questions / discussion points (things to decide before pilot):
- Bandwidth of dedicated reserve: do we commit 1 or 2 GPUs per 1k active users? (Cost/benefit model needed)
- How aggressive should automated fallback be for quality vs latency tradeoffs? (policy thresholds)
- Customer-facing SLA language: what do we promise for micro‑beta customers w.r.t. incident windows?

Quick links & references:
- Confluence playbook (detailed): confluence://prodops/microbeta-playbook-2024
- Raw telemetry sheet with historical baselines: drive://product-ops/microbeta‑telemetry‑2024 (link out to sheet)
- Incident runbook starter: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/blob/main/microbeta_incident.md

Notes from last sync (2024-12-10):
- Observed slightly higher token cost for long tail prompts in test cohort — Ravi to provide suggested quantization matrix by 12/13.
- Elena validated trace tags but found sampling rate too low for specific customer flows; increasing sample to 1% for those routes.
- Priya added 40 new sentinel prompts to cover hallucination modes seen in closed alpha.

Next actions (owners + ETA):

- Update customer comms templates with explicit fallback behavior — Ava — 2024-12-14
- Add cost anomaly alert (PagerDuty + Slack) to monitoring playbook — Marcus — 2024-12-12
